design.summary:
I measured the reference's visual design system from pixels. Every frame was cropped to the real picture area (x43-1039, y59-1828 of the recording, exactly 9:16) and scaled to 1080x1920, and all numbers below are in that space. The full report is at /home/user/abdulrahmanalharbi1/filmx-ref/analysis/design.md, with evidence images in /home/user/abdulrahmanalharbi1/filmx-ref/work/design/.

**The stage.** Every light scene uses one static set:
- Warm paper #FEFCF6 (almost the same as FILMX ivory #FBFAF7).
- A tall soft vignette: sides about 6-8% darker, corners about 35-40% darker.
- A faint dashed grid: 140px cells, 18px dashes with 13px gaps, about 2px thick, colour about #DCDAD5. It is centred on the frame and only visible inside a soft oval of about 760x830 px around (540,905).
- A matte charcoal leaf fan in the top-left corner (#252525, about 31% of width x 16% of height) and a blurred copy in the bottom-right.
- A static black header logo, 300x96 px, top at y=100.

**Typography.**
- The font is Montserrat with tight tracking.
- Each card has 1-4 short lines: small Medium-weight lead-in words (41-54 px) sitting on a hero word (100-120 px) or a mega word (160-364 px).
- The topic word is a big grey gradient (#5E5E5E at the top to #969696 at the bottom). The claim or payoff line is warm black #1C1A18 or pure black.
- The gap from one line's baseline to the next line's cap-top is a constant 16-25 px, whatever the size.
- The strikethrough bar is 0.13em thick, sits at mid cap-height and overhangs the word by 0.35em on each side.
- Pills are 76px tall, #424040 with #E5E5E5 text, radius about 8-10px, 136px apart, with a soft shadow.

**Layout.** Side margins are about 100px. Text sits between 22% and 55% of the height, and objects sit between 40% and 92%, often overlapping the last text line or running off the edge. Nothing is placed below 85.7% of the height.

**Objects.** All objects are fully grey (no colour): glossy black or chrome renders, black-and-white photos, and one flat paper-cut figure. The main light comes from the upper-left and shadows fall right and down, as a tight contact shadow plus a wide soft one. A blurred copy of the object often sits in the opposite corner for depth.

**The one accent colour.** At the climax (about 0:29.2) the frame burns from maroon #3B1016 to coral #FB9468, flashes white, then a copper wash (#A45E2B) fades into a dark end card (#1A1A1A). The end-card logo is 59% of the width, with a grotesque-font tagline in #D4D4D4 and the URL in #989797 at 93-95% of the height.

**True edit order.**
1. We don't start with Ads (rocket)
2. We start with Clarity (magnifier)
3. Most Marketing Conversations Begin here (paper-cut silhouette)
4. Budget
5. Platforms
6. Campaign ideas
7. But before ads...
8. 3 things + 3 pills
9. Without those Answers (statue)
10. Ads don't create Growth, with Growth struck through
11. They create Activity (puzzle)
12. Clarity turns marketing into leverage (seesaw)
13. Accent burn
14. End card

The "We Don't Start With Ads" layout seen at 35.6s is the cover (poster) frame shown at the loop point. The linear bottom darkening that starts at 85.7% of the height is most likely the player's control shading, so it should not be copied.

**For FILMX.** The palette carries over almost directly: ivory paper, ink #1C1B18, a warm-grey hero gradient, and gold #8A6E3F/#C9A86A as the only accent. The earlier storyboard's red stamp colour should be replaced by an ink strikethrough. For Arabic, sizes go up about 1.15x, Arabic is never letter-spaced, and the side-column layout is mirrored for right-to-left. Offers and warranties fit the pill list, but their content has to come from FILMX's real terms and is left as placeholders. The report also describes 4 prototype directions of 5 seconds or less.

principles.name: One static stage for the whole film
principles.rule: All light scenes share one fixed plate that never changes between scenes, and only text and objects change on top of it. The plate is: paper #FEFCF6 at the centre; a soft rounded vignette (sides only 6-8% darker at mid-height, e.g. L206 at x=0,y=1400; top corners about 35-40% darker, L~153-181); a centred dashed grid; corner foliage; the header logo at a fixed position. Sampled background values match within ±1 level across scenes.
principles.evidence: Identical background samples at t13.3, 14.8, 17.0 and 20.5 (e.g. (540,1450)=#FEFCF6, (1060,300)=#B5B5B0). Median plate across 13 scenes: work/design/bg_median.png. The logo and grid persist from 0:00 to 0:29.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Build one FILMX stage layer: ivory #FBFAF7 centre, multiplied by a warm vignette toward #D8D3C7 at the sides and #B9B2A3 in the corners. Render it once and keep it under every scene. Change only text and objects per beat.

principles.name: Architectural dashed grid, masked to an oval
principles.rule: Square grid with 140 px cells (13% of width). Vertical lines at x=325/470/610/749, horizontal at y=684/824/963/1102/1241, so it is centred on the frame. Dash 18 px on / 13 px off, stroke about 2 px, dashes cross as '+' at intersections. Peak colour is about 12% darker than the paper (L220 on L249, ~#DCDAD5). It is visible only inside a soft ellipse of about 760x830 px centred at (540,905) and fades to zero at the edge. It sits behind everything and never animates.
principles.evidence: Column/row darkness peaks in t13.3 and the dash run-length pattern on x=470. Close-up: work/design/zoom_grid.png. Contrast drops to 0 at x<150, x>910, y<490 and y>1320.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Draw the grid in FILMX hairline #D8D3C7 at about 55% opacity, 2 px, dash 18/13, cells 140 px, with a radial mask 760x830 at (540,905). It supports the 'architectural' brand tone directly.

principles.name: Small lead-in plus huge hero word
principles.rule: Each card is 1-4 short lines. Lead-in words are Medium weight at 41-54 px (2.2-2.8% of height). Bridge or assertion lines are 80-85 px (4.3% of height), Bold or ExtraBold. Hero words are 100-120 px (5.2-6.2%). Mega words are 160-364 px (8.5-19%). The hero is 2.5x the lead-in; mega words are 3.8-6.7x. Hero words fill 40-65% of the frame width, and no line exceeds about 80% of the width.
principles.evidence: Opening 'Ads' cap 255 px (~364 px size) with 'We don't' cap 38. 'Clarity' 163 / 'Turns marketing' 43 / 'Into leverage' 83. '3 things' 119 / 'Need to be clear' 50. 'Budget' 117. Ruler crops: work/design/r_ads.png, r_clar.png, r_mkt.png, r_growth.png.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: IBM Plex Sans Arabic, about 1.15x the Latin sizes: lead-in 50-58 px Medium, bridge 90-96 px Bold, hero 120-140 px Bold, mega word 240-320 px Bold (width at most 864 px). Keep 1-4 lines per card and one idea per card.

principles.name: Grey means topic, black means verdict
principles.rule: The word being questioned (the topic) is set huge in a grey vertical gradient: top #5E5E5E-#696768 to bottom #909090-#979594, about 40 levels lighter at the bottom. The claim or payoff is solid near-black: #1C1A18, or #000000 in the later scenes. A card usually has one grey mega word and one black payoff line. The grey word reads by size, not by contrast.
principles.evidence: Stem colour profiles: 'Ads' #696768 to #909090 (t25.2), 'Marketing' #5D5B59 to #979594, 'Clarity' #7A7877 to #918F8E. Black lines include 'Conversations' #1C1A18 and 'Growth', 'Activity' and 'Into leverage' at #000.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Myth or topic words (e.g. الرخيص, اللمعة) get a warm-grey gradient #5E5A52 to #A39C8E. Verdict lines get ink #1C1B18. Only the single FILMX promise word (e.g. الأصلي or الضمان) may use the gold gradient #8A6E3F to #C9A86A instead of grey.

principles.name: Stacked lines with a constant gap
principles.rule: Lines are stacked as one tight block. The distance from one line's baseline to the next line's cap-top is 16-25 px (about 1% of height), whatever the font sizes. There is no paragraph spacing. Stacks are either centred on x=540 or left-aligned together on one edge.
principles.evidence: Clarity to Turns: 16 px. Turns to Into: 19. Marketing to Conversations: 20. Ads to Don't: 25. Don't to Growth: 21 (t30.6, t1.5, t25.2).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Stack Arabic lines with about 20-28 px between the baseline and the next line's top (line-height about 1.05-1.15). Check that the dots of one line do not hit the lam/alif ascenders of the next line.

principles.name: Split lead-in around a mega word
principles.rule: For the hook, split the lead-in into two short fragments placed at the top-left and top-right shoulders of a mega grey word. The fragments are about 54 px Medium in #5F5D59; the mega word is about 364 px with a cap of about 13% of frame height. The hero object flies in and overlaps the mega word's baseline.
principles.evidence: 'We don't' at x 280-475 and 'start with' at x 690-896 sit above 'Ads' (x 190-891, cap 642-897). The rocket nose touches the 's' baseline at y≈890 (t36.2).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Hook card for right-to-left text: the first fragment at the top-right shoulder, the second at the top-left, a grey mega word such as 'PPF' or 'الأصلي' between them, and a glossy fender or film roll crossing the word's baseline.

principles.name: Strikethrough in ink, not a second colour
principles.rule: 'Wrong' is shown with a solid bar in the text colour. Thickness is 0.13em (14 px at 107 px), centred exactly at mid cap-height, overhanging 0.35em (about 7% of the word width) on each side, with square ends. The struck word is heavy black.
principles.evidence: 'Growth' (t25.2): bar at y 788-801, x 252-853; glyphs x 288-813; cap 757-832, whose midpoint is 794.5.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: For fake-PPF claims, strike the Arabic word with an ink #1C1B18 bar 0.12-0.13em thick at about 0.28-0.32em above the baseline, overhanging 0.35em, drawn right to left. Drop the red stamp colour #7A2E24 so the only accent stays gold.

principles.name: Pill chips for lists (offers and warranties)
principles.rule: Chips are 76 px tall (4% of height) with a corner radius of about 8-10 px. Fill #424040, text #E5E5E5 Medium at about 43 px, horizontal padding about 24 px (0.55em). Width hugs the text. Chips are centred on x=540, spaced 136 px apart (60 px gap), and appear one per beat under a title and grey sub-line. Soft ambient shadow of about 0 6px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.25). The widest chip keeps about 107 px side margins.
principles.evidence: t20.5 pills at rows 762-837, 898-972 and 1033-1108; widths 587, 604 and 868; the paper darkens about 30 levels within 5-20 px around each pill. Ruler crop: work/design/r_pill.png.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Use these chips for FILMX offers, warranties and services: fill #2A2824, ivory #FBFAF7 text in IBM Plex Sans Arabic Medium 46-50 px, and an optional 1 px gold #8A6E3F border on the single key item (the warranty). Content must come from FILMX's real terms; use placeholders until supplied.

principles.name: Text on top, object below, touching
principles.rule: Keep about 100 px (9.3% of width) side margins for text. Text sits in the band from 22% to 55% of height, at the top of that band when there is an object; text-only cards centre at 47-49%. Objects sit between 40% and 92% of height, with centres at 52-73% of height and 39-61% of width. The gap from the last baseline to the object is 0-150 px, and the object often overlaps the bottom 20-40 px of the text (object in front). Nothing goes below 85.7% of height, and nothing but the logo and foliage goes above 20% of height.
principles.evidence: Text tops at 432-752 px. Object centroids: seesaw (52%,53%), tiles (50%,61%), ring (61%,64%). The rocket overlaps 'Ads', the sphere covers 'Into leverage' and the lens magnifies 'Clarity'. Annotated frame: work/design/layout_annotated.png.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: The same bands suit TikTok and Reels safe areas. Keep Arabic text inside x 100-980 and y 420-1060, and place the car, film or roll objects so their top edge touches or slightly covers the last text line.

principles.name: Offset text column beside a figure
principles.rule: When the visual is a person or statue, left-align the text block at x 310-485 (29-45% of width) and let the figure fill the other half, bleeding off the side and bottom (up to 47% of the frame area). Put a light halo disc (#D2D2D2-#D8D8D8, about 12% darker than the paper) behind the figure's shoulder to separate it from the background.
principles.evidence: 'Without those / Answers' at x 483-985 beside the statue (t23.0), with the disc sampled at #D2D2D2 to #D8D8D8. 'Most / Marketing / Conversations' at x 410 beside the silhouette (t1.5).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Use this for the user's own presenter: a black-and-white, desaturated, high-key waist-up cut-out bleeding off the left edge and bottom, with a halo disc #E4E0D6 behind it. The Arabic text block is right-aligned with its right edge at x=980.

principles.name: Monochrome objects, one lighting setup
principles.rule: Every object is fully desaturated (red minus blue ≈ 0) and cut out onto the paper, which reads slightly warm around it. Materials are glossy piano-black, chrome, black-and-white photography, or one paper-cut illustration. Key light is a large soft source upper-left/front: softbox reflection at the upper-left of spheres, silver rim-light on the upper-left bevels. A single star glint appears where two glossy parts touch. Shadows have two layers: a tight contact shadow (8-15 px, 60-80% dark) and a wide soft drop (offset +20-40 px right and +30-40 px down, blur 60-100 px, 20-25% dark). Hero objects span 55-80% of the width, and tilts of ±10-15° or 45° add energy against the grid.
principles.evidence: Object red-minus-blue 0.1-0.6 vs paper 5.7-6.4. The cone shadow reaches about 100 px to the right vs about 60 px to the left. Beside the Google Ads tile the paper darkens about 55 levels, fading over about 100 px. Glint at the tiles' contact point (zoom_tiles.png, zoom_seesaw.png).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Render or generate PPF props in greyscale with the same lighting: a glossy black supercar fender with a peeling clear film edge, a chrome-core film roll, a squeegee, a magnifier over paint, a thickness gauge, a black metal warranty card, and a seesaw weighing a cheap roll against a genuine one. Add a star glint where the film meets the paint.

principles.name: Three depth planes with blurred echoes
principles.rule: Place a blurred copy of the hero object in the opposite upper corner (blur about 10-14 px, edge 30-40 px wide, 30-60% cut off by the frame). Put a blurred foliage element in the bottom-right, and use the sharp top-left foliage fan (matte #252525, about 31% of width x 16% of height, pivot off-canvas, slight sway) as the near plane. Hide the foliage in a corner that already holds a blurred echo.
principles.evidence: Blurred Visa card top-left (t9.5), blurred ∞ ring on the left (t12.2 and poster), bottom-right petals #6A6967 blurred. Top-left fan position changes between y 207 and 312 across scenes.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Replace the petals with a date-palm frond silhouette: ink at 90% top-left, and a blurred #8C877C copy bottom-right, swaying ±2-3° over 4-6 s. Add a blurred duplicate of the car panel or roll in the opposite corner.

principles.name: Static header logo, centred
principles.rule: The header logo is black (#0C0A08), centred, 300x96 px (27.8% of width, 5% of height), from y=100 to 196. It is identical and unanimated in every light scene, fades out only with the stage at the climax, and is absent from the cover frame.
principles.evidence: Median-plate bounding box x 388-688, y 100-196, centre x 538. Present from 0:00 to 0:29 and missing from the loop cover at recording 35.6 s.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Header block in the same 300x96 footprint: 'FILMX' in IBM Plex Sans SemiBold, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.30em, about 46 px, ink colour; a gold hairline #8A6E3F 72x1.5 px; then the Arabic tagline 'العناية الفاخرة وتخصيص السيارات' at 20-22 px in #6B665D. Keep it static throughout.

principles.name: One accent colour, only at the climax
principles.rule: About 99% of the runtime is warm paper, neutral greys and warm black. The single accent appears for under 1 s just before the end card. First, a gradient-map burn over about 0.2 s: shadows to #3B1016, then highlights to #FB9468 / #D9785A. Then a 1-2 frame white flash (#FDFDFD), then a copper wash #A45E2B (hue about 25°, saturation about 0.5) that fades to charcoal over about 0.3 s while the logo glitches in.
principles.evidence: Frames o31.47-o32.00: background #D9D1CF, then #EFDDD8, then #FBEBE3; cone #370E18, then #AA4D42, then #FB9468; flash #FDFDFD at 31.67; wash #583B26, then #8F562D, then #543926 (work/design/accent_strip.png, sheet_end.png).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Gold burn: shadows to #3A2C14, mids to #8A6E3F, highlights to #C9A86A over 0.2 s; an ivory #FBFAF7 flash for 2 frames; then the ink end card with a #8A6E3F wash at 35% fading over 0.4 s. Use no other colour anywhere in the video.

principles.name: Dark end card
principles.rule: Background #1A1A1A-#222222 with a faint concentric swirl (±4 levels), a little darker toward the bottom. White logo 59% of the width (x 222-859, y 812-1024). Tagline directly under it (y 1050-1090, about 42 px, grotesque font, #D4D4D4). The logo and tagline block is centred at about 49.5% of height. URL at 93-95% of height (y 1789-1828) in #989797. The logo glitches in over about 0.4 s, holds about 2.8 s, then fades to black over about 0.6 s.
principles.evidence: t33.5 measurements, end-card bounding boxes and colours; logo fragments visible from 31.8 to 32.4 s (sheet_end.png); fade out from 34.8 to 35.5 s (sheet_loop.png).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Ink #1C1B18 card with a faint radial swirl. Ivory 'FILMX' about 120 px with +0.30em tracking (56-60% of width) at y≈900. Gold #C9A86A hairline 120x2 px about 40 px below. Arabic tagline 40 px in #D8D3C7. Handle, phone, location or URL at y 1790-1830 in #8C877C.

principles.name: Cover frame as its own layout
principles.rule: The loop cover is a separate composition with no header logo and no foliage. It has a 3-line Title Case stack, left-aligned (x≈133-207): lead-in, a heavy black middle line, then a grey mega word (cap about 200 px). The hero object bleeds off the bottom-right, and a blurred echo sits top-left. The cover is neutral grey, without the warm paper tint.
principles.evidence: Frame at recording 35.62 s (crop/poster.png): 'We Don't / Start With / Ads', with the ∞ office ring bleeding off the frame.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Design the TikTok cover separately: a right-aligned Arabic 3-line stack (lead-in, ink line, grey or gold mega word), with the glossy car or film roll bleeding off the bottom-left and a blurred echo top-right.

motion.summary:
The reference is a 30fps ad, 33.25s long, recorded as a VFR screen capture. The recording starts parked at video 0:05 (the silhouette shot); at rec 1.75–1.85 the user scrubs back to 0:00, the player freezes until rec 2.20, and from there it plays straight through, so video time = rec − 2.20s (checked against six on-screen timecodes). That explains the apparent "repeat" around 6–9s. At rec 35.58 the player shows its poster frame for about 0.15s before looping; the poster is not part of the edit.

**True edit order (vt, video seconds):**

principles.name: One continuous set, refocused (rack-focus cut)
principles.rule: Keep one persistent background set across all beats (paper colour, dashed grid, vignette, corner prop, locked logo bug). Change beats with blur-out, cut, blur-in. Out: Gaussian blur sigma 0→~17px@1080p over 8–10 frames@60 (4–5 source frames), opacity stays >=90% (no fade). Cut on the peak-blur frame. In: the new plate starts at sigma≈17px and resolves in 8–12 frames. Text lines resolve later on their own stagger.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Build one ivory FILMX set: #FBFAF7 paper, #F2EFE7 edge vignette with a darker bottom 12%, hairline #D8D3C7 dashed grid at 30–40% opacity (cell 13% W ≈141px, dash 12 / gap 8), FILMX wordmark bug locked top-centre (≈28% W, top at 5% H), and one corner prop (a soft plant or car-silhouette shadow). principles.name: Two-tone, three-tier kinetic typography that doubles the VO
principles.rule: Tier A lead-in: Regular, near-black, 2.2–2.7% H. Tier B hero concept word: ExtraBold, mid-tone, 47–50% W and 7–11% H (the largest thing on screen). Stagger is 6–7 frames within a tight phrase, 10–19 frames for list-like lines, or VO-paced at 0.7–0.9s. A line reaches full opacity 0.2–0.4s before its word is spoken.

audio.summary:
I analysed the reference's audio. The main limit is that the web player was muted until rec 21.65, when the cursor clicks the speaker icon. So only the second half of the ad is audible, about 42% (vt 19.45 to 33.25 with vt = rec - 2.20, plus vt 0.00 to 0.94 on the replay). The sound before that is not the ad: a 3.1 kHz whine, low rumble and faint tones, with no speech. Whisper only hallucinates on it.

- **Voice-over.** It is English, and it reads the on-screen text word for word: "Without those answers / ads don't create growth / they create activity / clarity turns marketing into leverage", and on the replay "We don't start with ads". Auto language detection gave English at 0.945; forcing Arabic returned the same English words. The voice is calm, dry and close to the mic. Median pitch is about 150-158 Hz. Pace is about 4.6 syllables per second inside a phrase, about 105 words per minute overall. Phrases last 1.1-2.5 s, with 0.6-0.9 s breaths between them.
- **Music.** A sparse pulse bed at 92.9 BPM: soft hi-hat/shaker ticks every 0.323 s, a soft plucked note on every beat (0.646 s), and a held pad. There is no kick, no snare, no build and no drop. It sits about 11 LU under the voice (VO section -29.0 LUFS, music-only -40.1 LUFS). The music is never pulled down under the voice.
- **Cuts.** They are placed in the voice's breaths, not on the beat: only 2 of 5 land within 70 ms of a beat. Each new shot appears about 0.3 s before its line. Text leads the voice: the first line of a shot appears with the voice, and hero words appear about 0.4 s early (0.3-0.7 s).
- **Sound effects.** Only 2 designed sounds in 13.8 s of audio:
  - a short swish on the act-break whip. It has a 150 ms bright burst with a 4.3 kHz ping peaking on the cut frame, then a tail falling about 4 semitones over 250 ms.
  - a 0.7 s noise swell that peaks as the end-card logo starts writing on (rec 31.85-31.95), then cuts off within 0.15 s.

  The blur cuts, the crash-zoom, the strikethrough, the text reveals and the logo glitch are all silent.
- **Ending.** No voice over the logo. After about 2.4 s of music alone, the music fades about 15 dB over 0.8 s together with the picture fade, and goes silent about 0.2 s before black.
- **Opening.** The voice starts 0.08 s after the first frame, and the music starts with it.

For FILMX I recommend 90 BPM, so a beat is exactly 20 frames at 30 fps. The report includes a frame-by-frame audio template for the four prototypes of 5 s or less (150 frames each), mix targets (-14 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP or lower), and a recording guide for the user's own voice in Saudi dialect. It also suggests replacing the swish and swell with car-care sounds: a squeegee swipe and a heat-gun hiss. The advice for the offers and warranties list is inferred, because the matching part of the reference (the 3-pills list) was muted.

principles.name: Cut in the VO breath (VO-led edit, not beat-led)
principles.rule: Record VO with 0.6-0.9 s breaths between phrases (~1 beat). Place each shot change 0.35-0.45 s after a phrase ends and 0.18-0.32 s before the next begins; a fast transition (whip/crash-zoom) may start on the last syllable (-0.1 s). Do not force cuts onto beats: only 2/5 reference cuts are within +/-70 ms of a beat, and a constant 8th-note hat masks any +/-160 ms offset.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Have the user record each Arabic line as a separate take with ~0.7 s silence; lay lines first, then drop every rack-focus/whip cut 10-14 frames (@30) after a line ends. Cut the picture to the voice, and let the hats make it feel on-beat.

principles.name: Picture leads voice
principles.rule: The first frame of each new shot appears 0.15-0.8 s before its VO line (median 0.3 s = 9 f @30 fps). Never start a line on the same frame as the cut except the very first frame of the video.
principles.evidence: statue in rec 21.87 -> VO 22.35; Ads shot 23.78 -> 'Ads' 24.10; puzzle 25.97 -> 'They' 26.15; seesaw 27.55 -> 'Clarity' 28.35

principles.name: On-screen text = VO verbatim, and text leads the word
principles.rule: Kinetic text is the exact transcript. The first line of a shot appears 0-3 frames before the VO onset; hero or secondary lines appear 0.3-0.7 s (median 0.4 s = 12 f @30) before the word is spoken; the whole card completes before the sentence ends. Text never appears after its word.

Key the hero words (e.g. the warranty term, 'أصلي/تقليد') 12 frames ahead of the user's spoken word. For offers and warranties, each pill enters about 10-12 frames before its line.

principles.name: Minimal pulse music bed
principles.rule: ~93 BPM (use 90 BPM for frame-exact 20-frame beats @30 fps). Soft hat or shaker on every 8th (burst ~85 ms, ~200 ms tail, on-beat hats ~+8 dB), soft pluck or felt keys on every quarter in 250-600 Hz, and a sustained pad under 1 kHz. No kick, no snare/backbeat, no riser-drop, no melodic hook. Energy stays flat for the whole body.
principles.evidence: hat grid 0.32289 s fitted over 38 intervals, rec 22.231-34.501 (residual <=13 ms); 250-600 Hz attacks +8..+21 dB on beats only; 40-100 Hz shows no beat-locked rise; pad partials ~247/310/523/587/785/987 Hz
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Brief the music as: 90 BPM, felt piano or muted nylon/oud-harmonic pluck on quarters, warm low string pad, brushed shaker on 8ths, no drums or drop. This matches Old Money restraint better than trendy TikTok beats. Use the same bed for all 4 prototypes so the choice is about visuals only.

principles.name: Constant bed 11 LU under VO, spectrally carved, no ducking
principles.rule: Music bed sits ~11 LU below the VO and stays constant: no sidechain ducking. VO owns 250 Hz-2 kHz (+11 to +15 dB over the bed). The bed lives <700 Hz (pad/pluck) and >5 kHz (hats); keep 1-4 kHz of the bed empty.
principles.evidence: VO+music -29.0 LUFS vs music-only -40.1 LUFS; octave diff 250 Hz +11.3, 500 +14.7, 1k +13.0, 2k +12.9, 4k +6.4, 8k +5.3 dB; beat-hat peaks -44/-45 dB under VO = -45 dB in the VO-free end card

principles.name: SFX budget: silence on routine moves

principles.name: Whip swish spec
principles.rule: 150 ms bright burst (3-10 kHz) with a short tonal ping (~4.3 kHz, 110 ms), peaking on the cut frame (+/-1 frame), followed by a 250 ms tonal tail falling ~4 semitones (6.3->5.0 kHz). principles.name: Logo swell spec
principles.rule: Noise swell in 250-1500 Hz (noisy, spectral flatness ~0.2-0.28), rising ~17 dB over 0.7 s during the accent burn. principles.name: Outro choreography

principles.name: Hook at frame 0
principles.rule: The VO starts <=0.1 s (<=3 f @30) after the first frame, with music from frame 0: no intro sting, no silence. The hook line is the loudest VO of the piece (~+2 LU over the body VO).

principles.name: VO delivery profile

principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Build all 4 prototypes on this same audio template, with a temporary guide VO clearly marked as temporary or captions only. The user then judges only the visual direction, and their own recording drops straight into the same phrase windows (phrase 1 ≈1.3 s, phrase 2 ≈1.6 s).

narrative.summary:
I rebuilt the true edit order of ref.mov and transcribed every on-screen text beat, then mapped the same persuasion structure onto a FILMX video. The full report is at /home/user/abdulrahmanalharbi1/filmx-ref/analysis/narrative.md.

**How the edit order was recovered:** the player chrome was ignored. Recording 0–2.2 s is the user parked on video 0:04–0:05, then scrubbing back to 0:00. From rec 2.20 the ad plays straight through, so video time = rec − 2.20 s. The ad is 33.25 s long. The frame at rec 35.60 is the player's poster frame, and the loop restarts at rec 35.73. Audio is muted until rec ≈21.7. Where the VO is audible it repeats the on-screen words exactly, so the earlier VO is assumed to be verbatim too.

**The argument:** the whole ad is an "order of operations" claim built on two fixed nouns, repeated without synonyms:
- "Ads" (the enemy): on screen at 0.27, 10.6 and 21.67 s, plus the poster frame.
- "Clarity" (the hero): at 2.6 and 25.7 s.

**The seven acts:**

| Act | Time (vt) | Share | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contrarian hook | 0–3.77 | 11% | "We don't start with Ads / We start with Clarity": parallel syntax, one word swapped |
| Status-quo montage | 3.77–10.57 | 20% | "Most Marketing Conversations Begin here", then Budget / Platforms / Campaign ideas at 1.1–1.5 s each |
| Pivot | 10.57–12.25 | 5% | Typewriter "But before ads…" with the film's only still frame (0.9 s) |
| Checklist | 12.25–19.43 | 22% | "3 things / Need to be clear" plus 3 question pills: who, why you, what happens after |
| Stakes | 19.43–25.23 | 17% | "Without those Answers", then "Ads Don't create ~~Growth~~" (struck through), then "They create Activity" |
| Reframe | 25.23–29.53 | 13% | Callback: "Clarity Turns marketing Into leverage" |
| Brand | 29.53–33.25 | 11% | Logo, a tagline that restates the thesis, and the URL; no offer and no call to action |

**The visual metaphors:** each idea has one monochrome object that acts out the sentence's verb:
- rocket = ads
- magnifier = clarity (the lens sharpens the word itself)
- blank-sheet silhouette = conversations begin
- card = budget
- juggled app cubes = platforms
- busy infinity-shaped office ring = campaigns
- thinking statue = answers
- Meta and Google Ads tiles = ads
- puzzle = activity
- seesaw lever = leverage

Ideas the ad argues against get many objects; true ideas get one calm object. The pivot and the checklist get no object at all.

**Pacing:**
- Each line is readable 0.0–0.35 s before it is spoken.
- The "Growth" strike-through finishes about 0.15 s before the word is said.
- Cuts land 0.3–0.4 s after a spoken phrase ends.
- The voice slows down across the ad: about 4 words/s in the hook, about 2 words/s in the final line.

**FILMX adaptation:** the report gives a beat-by-beat Saudi-dialect script of about 40–44 s.
- Hook: «ما نبدأ بالسعر / نبدأ بالأصل». This is also literally true, because FILMX's site says it does not publish prices («لا ننشر أسعاراً»).
- Status-quo montage: «أغلب سوالف الحماية تبدأ من هنا» — الخصم / اللمعة / السرعة.
- Pivot: «بس قبل التركيب…».
- Checklist: «٣ أسئلة قبل ما تركّب» with pills «الفيلم صافي مثل الزجاج؟ / خدشه يختفي بالحرارة؟ / ووش يصير لو تضرر؟».
- Stakes: «بدون هالإجابات… الفيلم ما يعطيك ~~حماية~~… يعطيك لمعة مؤقتة».
- Reframe: «الأصل يحوّل الحماية إلى قيمة».
- New act, answer pills: FILMX's offers, sourced from filmx.capital and still to be confirmed by the client:
  - XPEL and Ravoony films
  - official warranty of up to 10 years, registered to the car's plate number
  - free replacement of any damaged piece, for any reason, with no conditions
  - 30-day installation warranty
- Optional montage of services.
- Gold-burn end card that signs off with «فيلم إكس… نبدأ بالأصل» so the video loops back to the hook.

The report also proposes four openings of 5 seconds or less for the user to choose between. It places the user's own voice on all lines and uses his face once, as a black-and-white cut-out in the status-quo beat. This follows the reference's rule of never showing a realistic face, which fixes the "unrealistic character" complaint.

principles.name: Contrarian parallel hook (negation then affirmation)
principles.rule:
Open with two beats that share the same syntax and differ by exactly one noun: '[We] don't start with <ENEMY>' then '[We] start with <HERO>'.
- Negation beat: ~1.6 s. The hero word resolves by +0.27–0.47 s.
- Then 0.4 s of empty set.
- Affirmation beat: ~1.8 s.
- Hook total ≤3.8 s (11% of runtime).
- The VO in the hook is the fastest in the film (~4 words/s).
principles.evidence: vt 0.00–1.60: 'We don't / start with / Ads' (lines at 0.00, 0.13, 0.27). Empty paper 1.60–2.00. vt 2.00–3.77: 'We / Start with / Clarity' (2.00, 2.27, 2.60). Loop VO 'We don't start with…' spoken in ~1.2 s.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: «ما نبدأ بـ / السعر» (gold hero, black price tag flying past), then 0.4 s of ivory paper, then «نبدأ بـ / الأصل» revealed inside a loupe over a clear PPF swatch. It is true to FILMX's no-published-prices policy.

principles.name: Two fixed nouns, repeated verbatim
principles.rule:
Choose one enemy noun and one hero noun in the first 4 s and never use synonyms.
- Repeat the enemy noun 3 times or more (hook, pivot, stakes).
- Repeat the hero noun 2 times or more (hook and reframe).
- The final argument sentence uses the hero noun as its subject.
principles.evidence: 'Ads' on screen at vt 0.27, 10.6 ('But before ads…') and 21.67 ('Ads don't create'), plus the poster frame. 'Clarity' at 2.6 and 25.7. 'Marketing' at 4.0 and 26.4.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Enemy «السعر» (hook), echoed by the montage and the pivot «بس قبل التركيب». Hero «الأصل» (hook, reframe «الأصل يحوّل الحماية إلى قيمة», and the VO sign-off «فيلم إكس… نبدأ بالأصل»).

principles.name: Order-of-operations vocabulary
principles.rule: Every act carries a sequence word. The thesis is 'do X before Y', so it sells a process, not a price.
principles.evidence: 'start with' (0.13, 2.27), 'Begin here' (4.63), 'But before' (10.6), 'Need to be clear' (12.7), 'Without those' (20.13), 'Turns … into' (26.4–27.4).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: «نبدأ» → «تبدأ من هنا» → «بس قبل التركيب» → «قبل ما تركّب» → «بدون هالإجابات» → «يحوّل… إلى».

principles.name: Seven-act persuasion arc with fixed proportions
principles.rule:
Act shares of runtime:
- Hook 11%
- Status-quo mirror 20%
- Pivot 5%
- Framework of 3 questions 22%
- Stakes 17%
- Reframe/callback 13%
- Brand 11%
The argument (pivot to reframe) takes 55% or more. The brand stays at 11% or less, with no offer or CTA verb in the reference.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: Keep each reference act at its absolute length and add one 'proof' act of the same length as the framework (≈7.2 s), plus an optional 3 s services montage. Total ≈40–44 s, under the 45 s cap.

principles.name: Status-quo mirror as a fast noun montage
principles.rule: Frame line ('Most … begin here', ~2.9 s, 4 staggered lines). Then 3 single-noun beats of 1.1 / 1.3 / 1.5 s, each with one literal object. Do not judge them yet; the speed itself signals noise.
principles.evidence: vt 3.77–6.67 'Most Marketing Conversations Begin here'. Budget 6.67–7.77, Platforms 7.77–9.03, Campaign ideas 9.03–10.57.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: «أغلب / سوالف الحماية / تبدأ من هنا», then «الخصم» (metal tag), «اللمعة» (many chrome spheres), «السرعة / كم يوم؟» (stopwatch).

principles.name: Typewriter volta with the film's only still frame
principles.rule:
A single conjunction line on empty paper.
- Hard cut in, no object.
- Typed at ≈2 frames (@60) per character.
- Then a 0.9 s fully static hold, then a hard cut out.
- Used once, at ~32% of runtime.
principles.evidence: vt 10.57–12.25 'But before ads…': typed 10.58–11.30, frozen until 12.18.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: «بس قبل التركيب…» typed RTL with a gold-light block cursor at the left writing edge, then a 0.9 s hold.

principles.name: Framework as 3 questions (the third is always 'what happens after')
principles.rule:
Numbered title ('3 things') plus a grey subtitle 0.45 s later. Then 3 question pills landing 1.5–1.8 s apart (+2.07, +3.90, +5.40 s) in one 7.2 s shot with no object.
- Order: who, why you, what happens after.
- This is the only place the viewer is addressed ('you').
principles.evidence: vt 12.25–19.43: pills 'Who exactly is the customer?' (14.32), 'Why should they choose you?' (16.15), 'And what happens after they show interest?' (17.65).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx:
«٣ أسئلة / قبل ما تركّب», then:
① «الفيلم صافي مثل الزجاج؟» (clarity test)
② «خدشه يختفي بالحرارة؟» (self-heal test)
③ «ووش يصير لو تضرر؟» (after-sale). ③ sets up the free-replacement offer.

principles.name: Stakes triad: condition, struck promise, substitute outcome
principles.rule:
Three statement beats of 1.9 / 2.2 / 1.4 s:
- 'Without those <answers>'
- '<Enemy> don't create <PROMISE>', with the promise word struck through
- 'They create <IMITATION>'
The strike is linear across ≈57% of the frame width over ≈0.6 s and finishes ~0.15 s before the VO says the word. The promise and the imitation form an antithesis pair.
principles.evidence: vt 19.73–21.53 'Without those Answers'. 21.60–23.77 'Ads / Don't create / Growth' with the strike 22.33→22.95 and VO 'growth' at 23.10. 23.80–25.17 'They create Activity'.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: «بدون / هالإجابات» (marble thinker with a loupe), «الفيلم / ما يعطيك / ~~حماية~~» (strike drawn R→L, unbranded yellowed roll), «يعطيك / لمعة… مؤقتة» (fake film whitening or tearing). Antithesis: حماية vs لمعة.

principles.name: Reframe = hero-noun callback transformation sentence
principles.rule: '<HERO> turns <category> into <benefit>' in three stacked chunks. Lines at +0.2, +0.9 and +1.9 s. This is the slowest VO in the film (~2 words/s). It is followed by ≈1.5 s of wordless object motion before the brand transition.
principles.evidence: vt 25.53–29.30: 'Clarity' 25.70, 'Turns marketing' 26.40, 'Into leverage' 27.40–27.80. VO 26.15–28.68. Lever-only tail to 29.25.
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx: «الأصل / يحوّل الحماية / إلى قيمة» (or «إلى راحة بال»). A lever made of a thin film sheet slowly lifts a heavy black car model.

principles.name: Question pills answered by answer pills (offers as proof, not promotion)
principles.rule:
Present the offers only as answers to the framework's questions, reusing the same pill component, positions and 1.5–1.8 s cadence.
- Answer pills: ink with a gold hairline and tick.
- Facts only: no prices, no 'limited time', no exclamation marks.
principles.evidence: The reference has no offer act; its pill grammar (vt 14.32 / 16.15 / 17.65) is the reusable component. The FILMX site offers are factual guarantees (see measurements).
principles.how_to_apply_to_filmx:
«في FILMX / الإجابة واضحة», then:

principles.name: One idea = one object performing the verb
principles.rule:
Each beat has exactly one monochrome object (glossy black, chrome, marble or paper-cut) that acts out the sentence's verb: launch, magnify, lift, strike, fit.
- Literal objects for tactics; classical symbols for principles.
- Plural objects for noise; a single object for truth.
- Pivot and framework beats have no object.

principles.name: Text leads voice; cuts sit in VO gaps; the VO decelerates
principles.rule:
Timing:
- A line is fully legible 0.0–0.35 s before its word is spoken.
- Cut 0.3–0.4 s after a phrase ends; start the next phrase 0.3–0.4 s after the cut.

SUMMARY: The official site https://filmx.capital (Arabic, RTL) is fully fetchable and is the authoritative source. It exposes server-rendered text, JSON-LD, /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt (a brand-authored fact sheet plus all blog posts). Scratch copies are in /home/user/abdulrahmanalharbi1/filmx-ref/work/research-web/ (home.html, page_*.html, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, index.js, sitemap.xml, tiktok.html, snap.html). Facts marked "medium" come from client-rendered page text in the site JS bundle (the Membership page, the Terms page, parts of the PPF, Tint and Wrap pages and the home hero). They are live on the site but are not in the server-rendered and llms text.

BRAND RULES THAT CONSTRAIN THE VIDEO SCRIPT (from llms.txt):
(1) Never state a price, price range or "starts from". Send viewers to WhatsApp or the booking form instead. "مجاناً" in the replacement pledge and "7 إلى 14 يوم عمل" in the refund policy may be said.
(2) Always list XPEL first. "10 سنوات" belongs to XPEL only. Ravoony may only be called «أفلام Ravoony الأصلية», with no nationality, agency, certification or warranty-duration claim, and only in a PPF context.
(3) Do not mention Tap, Tabby, Tamara or instalments.

OFFERS: The site publishes no dated promotion as of 2026-09-28. /Offers, /offers and /Warranty return 404. The standing offers are:
- Free replacement of any damaged PPF piece. This is the flagship pledge, framed as available only at FILMX in Riyadh.
- 7-day refund.
- Free car transport within Riyadh.
- Free consultation for wraps.
- The Founders Club VIP membership, labelled "عرض محدود", with the price given on contact.
Specific discounts are clearly handled privately: an "approved offer or discount" is locked with a non-refundable deposit. Anything time-limited must come from the client.

CONFLICTS AND STALE CONTENT, to confirm with the client before use:
- Hours. The current site-wide block says Sat 10am–10pm, Sun–Thu 2pm–10pm, Fri closed. Several older blog posts say Sat–Thu 9am–9pm.
- Payment. Older blog posts list Tap, Tabby, Tamara and instalments. The current rule says none of these are active.
- 30-year warranty. The client-rendered Terms page still shows "The 30-Year Promise / ضمان ذهبي لمدة 30 عاماً" on materials. This contradicts everything else (XPEL up to 10 years). Treat it as legacy and do not use it.
- Membership car coverage. One place says "all cars under your name", another says "up to 3 cars".
- Wrap materials. One legacy component says "3M أو Avery Dennison"; the current wording is 3M and KPMF.
- Stale search snippet. A search-engine summary said PPF "starts from 8,500 riyal" and that FILMX uses XPEL "exclusively". Both come from an older cached version of the site. The current site publishes no prices and lists XPEL + Ravoony, so do not use either claim.
- Brand-kit tagline. "العناية الفاخرة وتخصيص السيارات" does not appear on the website. The site uses "العناية الفائقة بالسيارات الفاخرة في الرياض" (title), "FILMX | العناية الفاخرة بالسيارات" (Google Maps name) and the slogan "حيث تُصان الفخامة بصمت".
- Tint brand. No tint brand is named anywhere; by the brand's own rule, Ravoony must not be linked to tint.

DEAD ENDS:
- Instagram returned HTTP 429 (blocked).
- TikTok profile data was retrieved, but video captions are not in the server-rendered page.
- The Snapchat profile exists (name FILMX) but has an empty bio.
- The Google Maps listing was not fetched (maps.app.goo.gl redirect). Its rating and reviews are not verified.
- No third-party directory or press coverage of the Riyadh studio turned up. Search results were competitors (Royet, Xtreme Nano, Johnson, etc.).

NAMESAKES RULED OUT (none are the Riyadh car-care studio):
- "فليكس فيلم / Flex Film": a car-services deal on Cobone for Jeddah.
- "FX Films / عوازل اف اكس": a carbon tint film brand.
- The FilmX entertainment app (mn.filmx.app on Google Play) and the FilmX YouTube movie channels.
- The FilmX Facebook pages (@FilmXapp, @filmxworld).
- A "FILMX" Webflow video-agency template.
- FILMX LTD, a UK company (Companies House).
- The FILMX ticker on Yahoo Finance.
- The Saudi Film Commission.
The Riyadh studio's official handles are filmx.sa (Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat); the domain is filmx.capital, not filmx.sa.

BRAND TONE: The site copy is calm, understated and "quiet luxury". Examples: "ما يصنع الفارق ليس ضجيج التسويق، بل انضباط التنفيذ" and "دليل هادئ وصريح". It stresses verifiable facts over hype ("بحقائق قابلة للتحقق دون مبالغة"), appointment-only exclusivity, documentation and warranties. This fits the Old Money brief.

MATERIAL FOR THE GENUINE-vs-FAKE VIDEO: The site's own talking points are:
- Genuine film has uniform thickness, self-heals and stays colour-stable. Unknown-source film yellows and shrinks within 1–2 years.
- Ask for a VIN-registered manufacturer warranty, not an internal certificate.
- Ask for the product certificate and its official source.
- The hot-water self-healing test.
- The six questions to ask any centre.
- FILMX tells you the brand and film type before installing.

maps.notes:
WHAT I CHECKED: I looked at maps, directories and dealer locators. I also read the official site, filmx.capital. It is fully fetchable, and robots.txt openly welcomes AI bots and points to /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt. Those two files hold FILMX's own 'mandatory rules' for any text written about them. The rules matter for the video script: no prices or 'starting from' figures, XPEL is always named first, Ravoony gets no nationality and no warranty duration, the 10 years belongs to XPEL only, and Tabby/Tamara/instalments are never mentioned.

GOOGLE MAPS: The short link maps.app.goo.gl/747Cix1qWxejVhGR8 opens the listing 'FILMX | العناية الفاخرة بالسيارات' (owner-verified; CID 0x3e2ee52930e28209:0xce63cd60150c3d37; KG /g/11zz0hmnjv). I parsed it from the /maps/preview/place JSON. That JSON has a 4.3 value in the rating slot but no review count, so treat the rating with medium confidence. The review endpoints (listugcposts / listentitiesreviews) returned 403/404, so I have no customer review quotes. Postcode mismatch: Maps shows 11432 and the site shows 13322. Current hours on Maps match the site.

XPEL AUTHORIZATION RISK FLAG (important for a 'genuine vs fake PPF' video): FILMX's FAQ says it is an authorized XPEL installer ('مركز معتمد لتركيب أفلام XPEL'). But FILMX is not on Zan Arabia's authorized-installer list. Zan Arabia is XPEL's exclusive Saudi distributor, and I checked the list on 2026-09-28. FILMX is also not on XPEL.com's Saudi installer pages; that locator may paginate, so this check is medium confidence. Viewers can check this on zanarabia.com. So the video should not say 'وكيل معتمد' or 'official XPEL dealer' until the client confirms it with Zan Arabia. The safe wording is 'أفلام XPEL الأصلية بضمان رسمي يصل إلى 10 سنوات مسجّل برقم السيارة', to be confirmed by the client. Zan's roll-number verification page (zanarabia.com/en/verification/) is a strong, verifiable 'how to spot genuine XPEL' tip for the educational part.

OFFERS: There is no price-based promotion anywhere. FILMX publishes no prices, and every service says 'السعر بعد التواصل'. The offers you can actually show are:
(1) Free PPF replacement for any cause for the whole warranty period, and this is also their current Google Business post.
(2) Free car transport within Riyadh.
(3) A 7-day refund policy.
(4) A free inspection/consultation.
(5) The Founders Club annual VIP membership.

The site says 'offers/discounts can be locked with a deposit', but no live discount is published. The Founders Club perks (3 PPF sessions a year, weekly tint and polish, 20% off) come from the client-rendered Membership page in the JS bundle. The server-rendered summary lists fewer perks, so the client should confirm them before they appear on screen.

INCONSISTENCIES:
- The blog price article says 'جميع الأفلام من XPEL' and elsewhere 'جميع الأسعار أعلاه خاصة بـ FILMX', although the table shows no prices.
- An old search-index snippet mentions Tabby/Tamara instalments, and the JS bundle still contains Tabby code. The current llms.txt says none of this is active.
- A search snippet says FILMX 'exclusively uses XPEL'; the current site says XPEL + Ravoony.

BLOCKED OR EMPTY:
- Instagram (login wall; the API returned 401 require_login).
- ravoony.com (empty reply / 502), so I could not check a Ravoony dealer listing.
- xpelme.com (connection reset).
- Google Maps reviews (403).
- filmx.sa, filmx.com.sa and filmx.salla.sa don't resolve, and salla.sa/filmx returns 410. I found no Salla/Zid store.
- No FILMX listing turned up on third-party directories, review sites, Cobone deals or in press.
- TikTok returned profile stats but no video captions.

NAMESAKES RULED OUT (none of them is the Riyadh studio):
- The FilmX movie app (Google Play mn.filmx.app, Mongolia) and FilmX YouTube/Facebook movie channels.
- The Webflow 'Filmx' video-agency template.
- The Yahoo Finance ticker FILMX (a mutual fund).
- FILMX LTD (UK Companies House 10207237).

TONE NOTES: The brand voice is calm and understated. It is certain without shouting ('حيث تُصان الفخامة بصمت', 'بالموعد فقط', 'دار حماية السيارات الفاخرة', 'استشارة هادئة'), heavy on terms and guarantees, and has no emojis or discount language on its own channels.

Each video page gave the caption, the on-screen 'stickersOnItem' text and createTime. I downloaded the videos, extracted frames and ran faster-whisper medium ASR. - Snapchat. The public profile __NEXT_DATA__ held Spotlight captions with upload dates, story snaps and 6 untitled highlights. I downloaded all 42 media files and read the frames.
- Instagram. The normal UA and the web_profile_info API returned 429/401. The crawler UA (facebookexternalhit) returned the meta bio and counts only. Posts were not reachable: imginn, picuki and urlebird are behind Cloudflare 403, and greatfon/dumpor is JS-only. The Instagram account is small (69 followers, 6 posts). Its bio ('Custom car wraps & protection / Premium only / احجز وخلك مختلف') reads older and more wrap-focused than the TikTok bio.

- The National Day 96 offer (full-body PPF from 6,996 SAR incl. VAT, per car, plus free piece replacement for the warranty period) is valid until 30 Sep 2026.
